issues.title: Unbound degree parameter in the Nevanlinna–Pick claim

failure_location.quote: Herglotz et. al. \cite{hesp:1991} proved that  the Nevanlinna-Pick interpolation exists and the minimal norm solution  $\|f\|_\infty$ is unique which is also rational with the degrees of both numerator and denominator  less than $n$ (see also \cite{lubr:2011,alyo:1983}).

issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims that the cited minimal-norm interpolant has numerator and denominator degrees less than n. The old paragraph actually specifies only ℓ interpolation nodes and gives neither an NP-specific n nor any relation between n and ℓ. Thus it does not support a meaningful degree bound in n; the bound must refer to the active node count ℓ.
issues.overall_effect: The introductory application contains a malformed quantitative degree guarantee, although no later formal result depends on it.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace “less than n” in the Nevanlinna–Pick degree claim by “less than ℓ,” the number of interpolation nodes.
issues.why_classification: The paragraph introduces exactly ℓ interpolation nodes and no Nevanlinna–Pick-specific parameter n. The surrounding statement uniquely forces the node count ℓ, so this is an isolated parameter transcription with no proof or dependent result to repair.

new_version_repair_locator.quote: with the degrees of both numerator and denominator  less than $\ell$

issues.title: Barycentric parameterization uses an undefined denominator variable
issues.failure_explanation: The theorem ranges over functions defined by eq:barycentricR, but that equation contains the unintroduced variable s in the denominator. With fixed s it is not the common x-dependent barycentric quotient and does not generally belong to $\scrR_{(\ell-1)}$. Replacing s by x restores the stated family.
issues.overall_effect: The literal statement of the cited barycentric parameterization theorem is undefined or false, although the later constrained barycentric formula is separately printed with the correct variable.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace s by x in every denominator of the denominator sum in eq:barycentricR.
issues.why_classification: The numerator, the function being defined, the preceding barycentric formula, and the claimed parameterization all uniquely require x. The unintroduced s makes the display ill-typed, but correcting it requires no change to the theorem’s argument or guarantee.

issues.title: Incomplete sample-set scope leaves the dual constructions undefined

failure_location.quote: Let  ${\cal X}:=\{x_j\}_{j=1}^{n+1}$. In this setting, we assume, without loss of generalization, that ${\cal X}\cap {\cal T}=\emptyset$.

issues.failure_explanation: The old disjointness condition covers only $x_1,\ldots,x_{n+1}$, whereas the objective and Cauchy matrices use $x_1,\ldots,x_m$. For an allowed case with $m>n+1$, choose the first n+1 samples disjoint from the support set and a later sample $x_j=t_k$. The old assumption holds, but entries $1/(x_j-t_k)$ in $C_p$ and $C_q$ are undefined, so the matrices A and B in Lemma lem:KKT do not exist. The same definition also causes the later extreme-point set to omit objective samples.
issues.overall_effect: The dual eigenvalue construction can be undefined for inputs admitted by the old setup, and the subsequent duality and active extreme-point results are not established for that stated domain.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define the sample set as X={x_j}_{j=1}^m, so the existing condition X∩T=∅ covers every sample used by the objective and Cauchy matrices and the later extreme-point set ranges over all objective samples.
issues.why_classification: Every objective, weight vector, and row of C_p and C_q is indexed through m, which uniquely forces X to contain all m samples. Replacing the copied upper index n+1 by m repairs the entire listed chain without changing any inference; the omitted collision cases could not coherently instantiate the displayed Cauchy constructions.

issues.title: Weak duality assumes an optimizer of the wrong primal problem
issues.failure_explanation: An optimizer of eq:bestf need not interpolate the prescribed values, so lem:baryrational2 cannot provide the barycentric feasible pair used in the comparison. Concretely, take $n=0$, $\ell=1$, $m=1$, $x_1\ne t_1$, $f_1=0$, and $y_1=1$. The unconstrained optimizer is $\xi^*=0$ with $\eta_\infty=0$, while the constrained barycentric family is the constant 1 and its normalized dual value is 1. Thus the claimed inequality $1\le0$ fails.
issues.overall_effect: Weak duality is false for positive ℓ under the printed hypothesis, and the later strong-duality proof and active extreme-point theorem lose their stated support.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change the hypothesis of thm:q-dual to require ξ* to solve the interpolation-constrained problem eq:baryInterpMinmax, and consistently use that constrained feasibility and barycentric parameterization in its proof. The resulting weak-duality bound then supplies the same support needed by the listed dependent results.
issues.why_classification: This is a local, routine repair that restores weak duality and its dependent chain with the intended conclusion and no new lemma or proof architecture. It is not merely a typo because the printed proof actually applies the constrained parameterization to an optimizer of the unconstrained problem, so a mathematical inference must be corrected.

issues.title: Strong-duality proof uses the wrong coefficient space
issues.failure_explanation: Equation eq:c2 gives $[\widehat a;\widehat b]=N\widehat c$, where $\widehat c$ has length $2n+2-\ell$. Since A and B in lem:KKT have $2n+2-\ell$ columns, $A^{\mathrm H}A-dB^{\mathrm H}B$ is a square matrix of that order. The old vector $[\widehat a;\widehat b]$ has length $2n+2$, so its quadratic form is dimensionally undefined whenever $\ell>0$. Using $\widehat c$ makes the subsequent weighted-residual equality valid.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of strong duality and complementary slackness is incomplete for the interpolation-constrained regime, and the active extreme-point theorem relying on it is consequently unestablished.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: For the competing barycentric pair, introduce the reduced coordinate vector ĉ satisfying [â; b̂]=Nĉ as in eq:c2, and replace both occurrences of [â; b̂] in the quadratic form by ĉ.
issues.why_classification: The dimensions of A and B and the already stated relation [a;b]=Nc uniquely force the quadratic form to use the reduced vector c. With that substitution, the same positive-semidefinite argument expands directly to the stated weighted-residual inequality, so no mathematical inference or downstream guarantee otherwise changes.
